label: Richard Boyd, How to be a Moral Realist §5.3: exceptions and proposed explanations
locator: reprint §5.3, p. 348: apparent failures of rational supervenience
interpretation: Primary source, the second numbered feature. Boyd explicitly says rational supervenience appears to fail for some actual cases and many counterfactual ones; he proposes unrecognized failures of bivalence in almost all such cases, and nonculpable methodological/theoretical shortcomings for others. These explanatory diagnoses are tentative ('plausible to argue', 'readily available') and do not exclude a properly specified determinate counterexample.
attribution: The passage states that apparent rational-supervenience failures occur in some actual and many counterfactual cases and offers non-bivalence or methodological/theoretical inadequacy as explanations, which is the proposal being recorded as the premise rather than an established exhaustive diagnosis.
